title: Workflow-Centered Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Repair Pipelines: Trace Quality, Canary/Rollback Outcomes, and Operational Reliability
research_question: In a simulated NetOps workflow with injected failures, how much does a generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage improve paired safe-deploy rates (guarded vs baseline LLM-alone) across a stress-test corpus of intents?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The paired safe-deploy rate under the guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair + canary) is higher than the paired safe-deploy rate under baseline LLM-alone proposals (estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline).
H2: The guarded pipeline with a canary stage will detect a greater share of injected latent failures pre-deploy (higher canary-detection rate) than a guarded pipeline without canary.
H3: When post-deploy regressions occur, workflows that emit proof-carrying audit traces will have higher automated rollback success rates than workflows lacking such traces.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do repair-iteration counts relate to eventual safe-deploy outcomes across injected-failure types?
E2: How sensitive are canary detection precision/recall and rollback success to canary-threshold settings and injection rates?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic topology corpus (public/open synthetic topologies only)
Challenging_workflow_stress_v1 task-index profile (included difficulty levels: very_hard, extreme)
Simulated digital-twin emulator used as deterministic validator (emulator implementation published with replay scripts)
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (difference in paired safe-deploy rates: guarded pipeline minus baseline LLM-alone)
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design with task_count = 1000 intents drawn deterministically using the provided challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile. Selection rule: for zero-based ordinal j from 0..999 set cycle=j//5, offset=[4,5,6,7,8][j%5], task_index=8*cycle+offset. This produces exactly 1000 unique task_indices. Each task yields two episodes (baseline and guarded). Planned model calls = task_count * 2 = 1000 * 2 = 2000 (one initial generation per task shared across paired conditions; guarded may use its single allowed repair call but adapter bounds model calls to exactly 2 per task). All seeds and task_index selection are fixed before any hosted-model invocation. Runtime sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, etc.) are recorded in the execution manifest per adapter rules.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute increase of 0.15 (15 percentage points). With baseline≈0.60 and guarded≈0.75, two-sided alpha=0.05 and task_count=1000 yields >80% power under the adapter/executor's McNemar-style paired test. The registered analysis executor will compute exact p-values and bootstrap 95% CIs (bootstrap implemented by executor). Sensitivity analyses vary baseline safe-deploy in [0.50,0.70] and repeat bootstrap CIs.
exclusion_rules: Tasks deterministically excluded by the preregistered challenging_workflow_stress_v1 index rule only (none additionally excluded post hoc).

If a task's initial generation contains evidence of prompt leakage (identical token-level traces across conditions beyond shared intent), the task is auto-flagged and excluded from sensitivity analyses but retained in the main intent set with the exclusion documented.
If the emulator returns a deterministic error for a candidate episode, that episode is flagged and handled per the missingness_plan and adapter/executor failure-treatment rules.
missingness_plan: Model/API failures or adapter infrastructure failures produce a recorded episode-level failure flag. Primary analysis uses the adapter's 'complete_pair_primary' treatment (executor documents how incomplete pairs are handled). Sensitivity analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' where any failed episode is treated as an unsafe outcome. All missingness reasons are logged; no manual imputation or human annotation occurs.
analysis_plan: Confirmatory analysis executed by the registered analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' using result schema 'paired_binary_episode_v1'. Primary test: McNemar-style paired difference test implemented by the executor for estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (primary_estimand_id = 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'); report absolute and relative improvement with bootstrap 95% CIs (bootstrap implemented by executor). Failed-call treatment: primary execution uses 'complete_pair_primary' per adapter contract; sensitivity analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'. Secondary analyses: paired proportion tests for canary detection and rollback success; exploratory time-to-recovery analyses are descriptive (Kaplan–Meier and log-rank where applicable). All analyses and seeds are executed by the registered executor; no human adjudication.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test is H1 (paired estimand above). Secondary estimands are reported with unadjusted two-sided p-values and bootstrap CIs; for hypothesis claims beyond the primary, multiplicity-adjusted p-values will be reported using the Holm–Bonferroni method in the analysis report. All tests and adjustments are preregistered.
contamination_plan: Benchmark names: challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus. Risk factors: leakage between baseline and guarded conditions via shared prompt materials or cached outputs; overfitting of canary thresholds to the simulated failure distribution; validator-emulator deterministic shortcomings (emulator blind spots). Detection procedures: deterministic seeding and fixed task_index selection pre-execution; automatic comparison of prompt texts and prompt-embedded context hashes between conditions to ensure independence; monitoring of per-failure-type prevalence and flagging deviations >5 percentage points from preregistered injection rates prior to analysis. Flagging rules: tasks with prompt-leak evidence are auto-flagged and handled as specified in exclusion_rules; emulator deterministic errors are flagged and treated per missingness_plan. Analysis treatment: flagged items are recorded and reported; main confirmatory analysis uses the full preregistered task set (excluding only tasks excluded by predeclared deterministic selection rules).
stopping_rule: Execute all preregistered task_count = 1000 paired episodes. If adapter or infrastructure failures prevent completion within the adapter/manifest constraints, stop execution and run the preregistered sensitivity analyses (including failure-as-zero). No post-hoc reduction of task_count is permitted except for deterministic predeclared selection rules or unrecoverable infrastructure failure, in which case the event and deviation are recorded and disclosed.
planned_outputs: Raw model outputs and validator/emulator traces
Analysis results (paired_binary_analysis_v1 output with bootstrap CIs)
Nearest-work comparison matrix and verified bibliography record
Complete IEEE LaTeX manuscript (≤5 pages) with Disclosure Statement
Execution code, replay scripts, and sanitized replay artifacts
Internal methodological, statistical-consistency, and reference-integrity reviews
Autonomous revision log and final-output hash manifest
